nodes.title: Vehicle record status = not in callers name or vehicle record s…?
nodes.comment: What arrives (contract v2, section 2). For a car that is not on the profile in use the identity agent returns the plate, the model and the facts, with an empty vehicle record id and record status not_in_callers_name (K12a, E53, E12) or not_found. An empty value is not known to replace an earlier one on its way back to the supervisor, so on a second car in the same call (E70) the record id of the first car could still arrive here. The record status decides: such a car is booked by plate and model, never by a record id, and every step below that reads the record (service history, recalls, warranty, last centre) tests the id and so stays away from it.

nodes.title: Booking router
nodes.comment: E52, E56, K11: the live booking check, from every channel, by plate. The booking system matches every filter it is given, so the plate alone finds each booking of this car, whichever phone made it. It runs before the centre is chosen and again directly before the booking is made (after the read-back), so a booking made online a minute ago is seen. The branch list below is the agent's routing table: first match wins. A branch carries only booleans and paths. Every text value is set at step level, in the small step the branch leads to: the compiler reads a quoted literal in a branch-level SET as a variable name.

nodes.comment: E56: "by plate and phone". A car on the profile in use is the caller's own car, and its booking is read out (E52). A car that is booked by plate only (a guest, a car not in the caller's name, a car that is not on the vehicle system) proves nothing about the caller: anyone can say a plate. Its booking is read out, and its confirmation sent again, only when the caller's number is the one on the booking, or the booking belongs to the profile in use. Otherwise the caller hears only that the car already has a booking, as a caller who books for the owner without the one-time code does, and a change is handed back.

nodes.title: Warranty tell
nodes.detail: Word what the caller is to hear about the warranty and write it to warranty_line: at most two short sentences, in the language the caller is speaking (English or Gulf Arabic), wor…
nodes.comment: Order of speech (contract v2, section 2): the request step that follows can finish in the same turn, when the centre and the number are already known, and the fixed lines after it would then be heard before a sentence spoken here. So this step words the dates in the caller's language, writes them to warranty_line and says nothing; warranty_say, a fixed step, says them, and the request step speaks after it. The step always ends after one pass and never waits for the caller: when nothing was written, warranty_fallback says in one fixed line that the centre confirms the dates and the cover.

A refusal by the booking system is a normal result with a reason: a slot that went leads to one more search (E85); a booking that is not allowed goes to a person.

nodes.title: Request tell
nodes.detail: Word what happens next for the caller and write it to request_outcome_line: at most two short sentences, in the language the caller is speaking (English or Gulf Arabic), worded ex…
nodes.comment: C2: details go to the team for imported cars, with the toll-free number. N03, Q05: the branch calls back. Q10: the service centre is in touch. Q12: a walk-in as the last resort. Order of speech (contract v2, section 2): a sentence spoken by this step would be heard after the fixed closing line that follows in the same turn. So the step words the outcome in the caller's language, writes it to request_outcome_line and says nothing; request_say, a fixed step, says it, and the closing line comes after it. The step always ends after one pass and never waits for the caller: when nothing was written, request_fallback says in one fixed line that the request has gone to the team.
